scope.title: Riskium An Ontology for Modeling Enterprise Risk Knowledge
scope.purpose: Model the content, context, provenance and relationships of enterprise risk knowledge to support structured analysis.
in_scope: Recorded treatment decisions, plans and control references
Recorded actors, responsibility and authority evidence
Evidence, observation results, indicators and thresholds
Criteria, appetite/tolerance statements and objective references
out_of_scope: Reconstructing complete ISO, COBIT or Risk IT frameworks
Designing organizational committees or RACI structures
Predictive risk accuracy or observed risk reduction without empirical evaluation
scope.source_use: Sources provide selected semantic anchors and contradiction screening. Missing out-of-scope process concepts do not constitute contradictions.
scope.claim_ceiling: No fundamental contradiction was identified in the inspected portions of selected sources; terminology differences and mapping restrictions are explicit. This is not a universal no-contradiction proof.

domains.title: Risk Phenomena
domains.definition: Risk-related subjects, specifications and explicitly referenced occurrences or conditions.
domains.objective: Preserve the distinction between what risk knowledge is about and the information expressing it.

domains.title: Risk Information
domains.definition: Managed information artifacts, their issued versions and the content they express.
domains.objective: Preserve documentary identity, interpretation and version lineage.

domains.title: Risk Classification
domains.definition: Governed vocabulary items, schemes and source-qualified classification assertions.
domains.objective: Organize risk content without confusing a term, its label and its referent.

domains.title: Risk Registration
domains.definition: Risk registers, entries, revisions, descriptions and recorded identification information.
domains.objective: Provide an advanced register representation with recoverable historical content.

domains.title: Risk Assessment
domains.definition: Information about assessments, their results, methods, scales, bases and uncertainty.
domains.objective: Support interpretation and comparison of results without prescribing an assessment process.

domains.title: Risk Treatment
domains.definition: Recorded treatment decisions, plans, action references and control information.
domains.objective: Connect decisions and reported actions to their evidential basis and risk subject.

domains.title: Risk Responsibility
domains.definition: Actor references and recorded responsibility or authority assignments, with optional grounded relationships.
domains.objective: Answer who was recorded as responsible, for what, and under which temporal and authority context.

domains.title: Risk Workflow
domains.definition: Recorded analysis and handling states under identified scheme versions and temporal assignments.
domains.objective: Preserve administrative history while keeping it distinct from real-world risk conditions.

domains.title: Risk Evidence
domains.definition: Evidence items and qualified references recording support, challenge or contextualization.
domains.objective: Preserve provenance and prevent an evidence link from automatically endorsing a claim.

domains.title: Risk Monitoring
domains.definition: Indicator specifications, observations, reported values, thresholds and signals.
domains.objective: Represent monitoring content and interpretation without designing an organizational monitoring process.

domains.title: Risk Policy
domains.definition: Recorded criteria, appetite and tolerance statements and references to objectives.
domains.objective: Preserve decision context and source-specific meanings without modeling a complete governance framework.

constraints.title: Risk Case is not ISO Risk
constraints.statement: Case identity is preserved across descriptions, scores, owners and administrative states. Equal labels do not establish case identity.

constraints.title: No realization from description
constraints.statement: A scenario, consequence statement, signal, plan or report alone must not create actual occurrences, outcomes, controls or effectiveness assertions.

constraints.title: Issued version immutability
constraints.statement: Issued semantic content and effective dependency versions are immutable. Correction and supersession create lineage-preserving new versions.

constraints.title: Assessment interpretation
constraints.statement: Results retain method/scale version, dimension, basis, relevant context and time semantics. A score is not the risk, and estimated likelihood need not be numeric.

constraints.title: Temporal and administrative distinction
constraints.statement: Recorded time, reference time and validity intervals are distinct. Workflow closure does not prove risk cessation or successful treatment.

constraints.title: Relator participant distinctness
constraints.statement: An asserted ResponsibilityRelator requires at least two distinct mediated individuals. If bearer and authority resolve to one actor and no further grounding exists, retain ResponsibilityAssignmentInformation without asserting the relator.

constraints.title: Role-qualified ownership
constraints.statement: ResponsibleAgentRole does not automatically mean Risk Owner. Ownership mapping requires recorded responsibility type, accountability, authority and applicable context.

constraints.title: Threshold anchor
constraints.statement: At least one of thresholdForIndicator or thresholdOnScale is present. If both are present, their scale/unit interpretation is compatible. Qualitative boundaries use scale semantics rather than invented numeric units.

constraints.title: Description aboutness
constraints.statement: Every published RiskDescription has at least one case, pattern or scenario target. Multiple valid targets are permitted and require explicit interpretation.

constraints.title: Framework-qualified tolerance
constraints.statement: Tolerance statements retain source framework/version, original meaning and context. Permissible deviation is not automatically equivalent to readiness to bear remaining risk.

constraints.title: Vocabulary resource identity
constraints.statement: Vocabulary resources retain scheme-qualified identity. Labels are representations and are not OWL classes by default.

constraints.title: Evidence does not endorse
constraints.statement: EvidenceReference states an evidential role such as support, challenge or context. Linking a source does not automatically prove the target claim.

constraints.title: Scale and dimension compatibility
constraints.statement: A selected level belongs to the selected scale version and dimension. Results on incompatible methods/scales are not ranked merely by equal labels or numeric codes.

constraints.title: Heterogeneous boundaries
constraints.statement: RiskSource, Consequence and RiskControl remain catalog notions and optional external boundaries, excluded from native formal-core class assertions. Source, outcome and control content is represented by RiskSourceReference, ConsequenceStatement and ControlReference.

constraints.title: Intrinsic vulnerability bearer
constraints.statement: Every asserted intrinsic Vulnerability has exactly one substantial-endurant bearer. A reported hypothesis alone is information, not an actual mode.

constraints.title: Admission profiles
constraints.statement: Raw source content is retained in staging. Managed records require identity, subject, title and provenance. Analytical readiness additionally requires the pinned context, method, scale, basis, dimension and time required for the selected task.

constraints.title: Multiple assertions
constraints.statement: Multiple classifications, descriptions, actors and evidence assertions are retained with role, context, provenance and time. Scalar export requires an explicit selection rule when several values apply.

constraints.title: Comparable assessments
constraints.statement: Direct comparison requires matching pinned method, scale, dimension, basis and temporal context; a governed explicit transformation may enable a different comparison. Missing data is not zero. Reported scores do not imply a reproducible computation.

constraints.title: Workflow semantics
constraints.statement: State labels are scheme/version qualified. Transition rules and authority are source-backed content. Missing rule means UNKNOWN; Closed does not imply ceased risk and Treated does not imply effectiveness.

constraints.title: Risk Item vocabulary
constraints.statement: In the terminology adopted by this profile, Risk Item denotes the managed risk subject modeled as RiskCase. This context-qualified mapping does not equate RiskCase with RiskRegisterEntry, RiskScenarioSpecification, ISO risk or any global Risk Item class.

constraints.title: Reported and computed scores
constraints.statement: A reported RiskScoreResult may have no derivedFrom links. A computed RiskScoreResult requires at least one linked DimensionAssessmentResult, a pinned method and adequate inputs. The score kind must be recorded.

constraints.title: Responsibility identity
constraints.statement: Repeated mandates between the same participants are permitted when grounding assignment, responsibility scope or validity differs. Duplicate representations of the same grounded mandate must resolve to one relator identity; participant equality alone is not an identity key.

constraints.title: Context relation coherence
constraints.statement: Every analyzedInContext link is also a hasContext link for the same RiskCase and RiskContextSpecification. The broader hasContext relation may include non-analysis context.

constraints.title: Revision coherence
constraints.statement: For each EntryRevision, revisionOf and inherited versionOf identify the same RiskRegisterEntry. previousRevision is irreflexive and acyclic and, when present, relates revisions of the same entry.

constraints.title: Version target coherence
constraints.statement: usesContextVersion targets a version of RiskContextSpecification; usesMethodVersion a version of AssessmentMethodSpecification; usesScaleVersion a version of AssessmentScale; usesCriteriaVersion a version of RiskCriteria. Artifact-level references, when present, agree with versionOf.
